sources.entry: Hammerdeck - Keyboard window manager for large and multiple displays, with grid placement, moves and swaps between displays, one-key undo, and rules that rearrange windows when a display connects.

summary.one_liner: Hammerdeck is a free, local-first macOS app that adds keyboard-driven window placement, grids, display-to-display moves and swaps, and a rules engine that rearranges windows when displays connect.
summary.what_it_does: Hammerdeck is a native Swift menubar app with an embedded Lua engine, aimed at large and multiple displays where macOS offers no built-in display-move shortcut. Its window features cover snapping to halves, toggling 75% size, saving custom placements, moving windows between displays, and swapping two displays' windows. Grid placement lets you name two cells so a window spans them, with 3×3, 2×2 and orientation-aware 6-cell grids. Window Mode is a modal keyboard layer for move, resize, corner and centre actions, while Window Deck tiles a screen's windows and enlarges the focused one, and Window Fan keeps an edge of each window reachable. Window Rewind undoes the most recent window rearrangement with one hotkey. A rules engine, configured in Settings without code, reacts to signals such as displays connecting, app launches, appearance changes and power source, and can run feature actions or macOS Shortcuts. Other catalog features include a command palette, window and browser-tab switchers, clipboard history, an app launcher, text actions, sleep and break helpers, and a Bing wallpaper. Optional extensions in Lua and a token-guarded local MCP endpoint for coding agents are also described.
use_cases: arrange windows across multiple monitors from the keyboard
place a window into a grid cell or spanning rectangle on an ultrawide
move a window or swap windows between displays with a hotkey
automatically rearrange windows when a display connects
switch between windows or browser tabs with a searchable list
notable: Grid placement by naming two cells, so one window spans a rectangle
Rules engine triggered by display connect, app launch, appearance and power changes, configured without code
One-key undo for window moves via Window Rewind
Extensions in Lua with declared, machine-checked capabilities
Local-only MCP endpoint for coding agents, off by default
